label: Thm_KKLM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\cite{KKLM17}\label{Thm_KKLM}
For any $h>0$ and any sequence $(\mu_k)_{k\geq1}$ of $a$-invariant probability measures on $X_{m+n}$ with $h_{\mu_k}(a)\geq h$, any weak$^\ast$ limit $\mu$ of the sequence satisfies
\[
\mu(X_{m+n})\geq h-(m+n-1).
\]
head: environment

label: Thm_main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Thm_main}
There exists a sequence of $a$-invariant probability measures $(\mu_k)_{k\geq 1}$ on $X_{m+n}$ with $\lim_{k\to\infty}h_{\mu_k}(a) = m+n-1$ such that its weak$^\ast$ limit is the zero measure.

label: Def_Temp
title: Definition
body_md:
An $m\times n$ \textit{template}\label{Def_Temp} is a piecewise linear map $\mathbf{f}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}^d$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_1\leq \cdots\leq f_d.$
\item\label{Temp_item_2} $-\frac{1}{n}\leq f_i'\leq \frac{1}{m}$ for all $i$.
\item For all $j=0,\dots,d$ and for every interval $I$ such that $f_j<f_{j+1}$ on $I$, the function
$\sum_{0<i\leq j}f_i$ is convex and piecewise linear on $I$ with slopes in the set
\[
\left\{\frac{L_{+}}{m}-\frac{L_{-}}{n}: L_{+}\in [0,m]_\mathbb{Z}, L_{-}\in[0,n]_\mathbb{Z}, L_{+}+L_{-}=j\right\}.
\] As a convention, we use $f_0 =-\infty$ and $f_{d+1}=+\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Template

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a template and $I$ be an open interval on which $\mathbf{f}$ is linear. 
An \textit{interval of equality} for $\mathbf{f}$ on $I$ is an interval $(p,q]_\mathbb{Z}$ with $0\leq p<q\leq d$ such that
\[
f_p<f_{p+1}=\cdots=f_q < f_{q+1}\ \text{on}\ I.
\]
For $0\leq p<q\leq d$ with an interval of equality $(p,q]_\mathbb{Z}$, we let $M_{\pm}(p,q)$ be the unique integers such that
\[
M_{+}+M_{-}=q-p\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{i=p+1}^q f_i' = \frac{M_{+}}{m}-\frac{M_{-}}{n}\text{ on } I.
\]
Note that $M_{\pm}\geq 0$ by \eqref{Temp_item_2} of Definition \ref{Def_Temp} (see page 24 in \cite{DFSU}). We also let
\[
S_{+}  = \bigcup_{(p,q]_\mathbb{Z}} (p,p+M_{+}(p,q)]_\mathbb{Z} \quad\text{and}\quad
S_{-} = \bigcup_{(p,q]_\mathbb{Z}} (p+M_{+}(p,q), q]_\mathbb{Z}
\]
where the unions are taken over all intervals of equality for $\mathbf{f}$ on $I$. Note that $S_{+} \cap S_{-} =\varnothing$, $S_{+}\cup S_{-}=[1,d]_\mathbb{Z}$, $\#S_{+}=m$, and $\#S_{-}=n$.
Define
\[\begin{split}
\delta(\mathbf{f},I) &= \#\{(i_{+},i_{-})\in S_{+}\times S_{-}: i_{+}<i_{-}\};\\
\underline{\delta}(\mathbf{f})&= \liminf_{T\to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T \delta(\mathbf{f},t) dt,
\end{split}\]
where $\delta(\mathbf{f},t)$ is the piecewise constant function with value $\delta(\mathbf{f},I)$ on $I$.
The value $\underline{\delta}(\mathbf{f})$ is called the \textit{lower average contraction rate} of $\mathbf{f}$.
head: environment
name: Contraction rate of a template

label: Thm_VP
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Thm_VP} 
For all $\epsilon>0$, there exists $C>0$ such that for every template $\mathbf{f}$,
\[
\dim_H(\mathcal{D}(\mathbf{f},C)) \geq \underline{\delta}(\mathbf{f})-\epsilon,
\]
where 
\[
\mathcal{D}(\mathbf{f},C) = \{A\in M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R}): \|\mathbf{h}_A-\mathbf{f}\|\leq C \}.
\]

name: Standard template

title: Remark
body_md:
As explained in \cite[Definition 9.1 and Lemma 9.2]{DFSU}, the formulas \eqref{Eq_ST1}, \eqref{Eq_ST2}, and \eqref{Eq_ST3} are necessary to ensure the existence of the standard template.
In particular, we will choose $t_k = kt$ and $\epsilon_k = C>0$ with some large $t >0$ and some constant $C>0$ for all $k\geq 1$, hence $\Delta\epsilon_k =0$. See the proof of Proposition \ref{Prop_dim}. Note that if $\Delta t_k = t$ is large enough compared to the constant $C$, the formulas \eqref{Eq_ST1}, \eqref{Eq_ST2}, and \eqref{Eq_ST3} hold unless $(m,n)= (1,1)$. If $(m,n)=(1,1)$, it follows from \eqref{Eq_ST2} and \eqref{Eq_ST3} that $\epsilon_k = \epsilon_{k+1} =0$. In order to choose $\epsilon_k = C>0$, we should assume that $(m,n)\neq (1,1)$.
head: environment

label: Prop_dim
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Prop_dim} Suppose that $(m,n) \neq (1,1)$.
For any $\epsilon>0$, there are constants $\rho_{\epsilon},\eta_{\epsilon}>0$ and $t_\epsilon\in \mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\dim_H \{A\in M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R}) : \rho_\epsilon \leq \lambda_1(a_t u_A\mathbb{Z}^d) \leq \eta_\epsilon \text{ for all }t\geq t_\epsilon\} \geq mn-\frac{mn}{m+n}-\epsilon.$$
Moreover, $\rho_\epsilon, \eta_{\epsilon}$ converge to $0$ as $\epsilon \to 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We will use the following notation: given any template $\mathbf{g}$ and interval $[T_1,T_2]$, we denote $$\Delta(\mathbf{g},[T_1,T_2]) = \frac{1}{T_2 - T_1} \int_{T_1}^{T_2} \delta(\mathbf{g},t)dt.$$

Fix $\epsilon>0$ and let $C_\epsilon>0$ be as in the statement of Theorem \ref{Thm_VP}. We may assume that $C_\epsilon \to \infty$ as $\epsilon \to 0$ by replacing $C_\epsilon$ with $\max(C_\epsilon, 1/\epsilon)$.
Fix large $t>0$ to be determined later. Define the template $\mathbf{f}$ by
\[\mathbf{f} = \begin{dcases}
\mathbf{s}[(0,0),(t,-2C_\epsilon)] & \text{ on } [0,t]\\
\mathbf{s}[(kt,-2C_\epsilon),((k+1)t,-2C_\epsilon)] & \text{ on } [kt,(k+1)t] \text{ for all } k\geq 1.
\end{dcases}\]
Note that if $t>0$ is large enough, then the formulas \eqref{Eq_ST1}, \eqref{Eq_ST2}, and \eqref{Eq_ST3} hold for all the above standard templates since $(m,n) \neq (1,1)$.

Following \cite[Section 9]{DFSU}, we have that for each $k\geq 1$
\[\begin{split}
\Delta(\mathbf{f},[kt,(k+1)t])&=\Delta(\mathbf{s}[(kt,-2C_\epsilon),((k+1)t,-2C_\epsilon)],[kt,(k+1)t])\\
&=\Delta\left(\mathbf{s}\left[\left(0,-\frac{2C_\epsilon}{t}\right),\left(1,-\frac{2C_\epsilon}{t}\right)\right],[0,1]\right)\\
&=\Delta(\mathbf{s}[(0,0),(1,0)],[0,1])-O\left(\frac{C_\epsilon}{t}\right)\\
&=mn-\frac{mn}{m+n}-O\left(\frac{C_\epsilon}{t}\right).
\end{split}\]
By Theorem \ref{Thm_VP}, $\dim_H(\mathcal{D}(\mathbf{f},C_\epsilon)) \geq mn-\frac{mn}{m+n}-\epsilon-O\left(\frac{C_\epsilon}{t}\right)$.
Take $t=t_\epsilon\in\mathbb{N}$ large so that $\dim_H(\mathcal{D}(\mathbf{f},C_\epsilon)) \geq mn-\frac{mn}{m+n}-2\epsilon$.

Fix any $A \in \mathcal{D}(\mathbf{f},C_\epsilon)$ and let $\mathbf{h}_A = (h_1,\dots,h_d)$. Observe that $$h_1(t) = f_1(t) - (f_1(t)-h_1(t)) \leq -2C_\epsilon + C_\epsilon = -C_\epsilon$$ for all $t\geq t_\epsilon$. Note that $\mathbf{f}$ is a bounded template. Setting $D_\epsilon = \max_{t} (-f_1(t))$, $$h_1(t) = f_1(t) - (f_1(t)-h_1(t))\geq -D_\epsilon-C_\epsilon$$ for all $t\geq t_\epsilon$. 
Hence, it follows that
\[\begin{split}
\dim_H\{A\in M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R}) :  -D_\epsilon -C_\epsilon \leq \log\lambda_1(a_t u_A \mathbb{Z}^d) &\leq -C_\epsilon, \forall t\geq t_\epsilon \}\\
 &\geq mn-\frac{mn}{m+n}-2\epsilon.
\end{split}\]
Since $-D_\epsilon -C_\epsilon$ and $-C_\epsilon \to -\infty$ as $\epsilon \to 0$, taking $\rho_\epsilon =  e^{-D_{\epsilon/2} -C_{\epsilon/2}}$ and $\eta_\epsilon = e^{-C_{\epsilon/2}}$, we can conclude Proposition \ref{Prop_dim}.

label: Prop_construction

label: rem_compact
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem_compact}
The set $\{x\in X : \rho_\epsilon \leq \lambda_1(x) \leq \eta_\epsilon \}$ is a compact subset of $X$ by Mahler's compactness criterion.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given $\epsilon>0$, let $\rho_\epsilon,\eta_\epsilon>0$ and $t_\epsilon\in\mathbb{N}$ be as in Proposition \ref{Prop_dim}. Denote 
\[
E(\epsilon)=\{A\in \mathbb{T}^{mn}: \eta_{\epsilon}\leq \lambda_1(a_t u_A \mathbb{Z}^{d}) \leq \rho_\epsilon \text{ for all }t\geq t_\epsilon\},
\] where $\mathbb{T}^{mn}=\mathbb{R}^{mn}/\mathbb{Z}^{mn}$ with the metric $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb{T}^{mn}$ induced by the supremum norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb{R}^{mn}=M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$. 
For each $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S_N$ be a maximal $e^{-(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1}{n})N}$-separated subset of $E(\epsilon)$. 
Since the value $\lambda_1(a_t u_A \mathbb{Z}^d)$ is invariant under $\mathbb{Z}^{mn}$-translations, i.e. $\lambda_1(a_t u_{A+Z} \mathbb{Z}^d)=\lambda_1(a_t u_A \mathbb{Z}^d)$ for any $Z\in\mathbb{Z}^{mn}$, it follows from
Proposition \ref{Prop_dim} that

\begin{equation}
{
\liminf_{N\to\infty} \frac{\log |S_N|}{(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1}{n})N} \geq \dim_H E(\epsilon) \geq mn-\frac{mn}{m+n}-\epsilon,
}\label{Eq_BoxDim}
\end{equation}

Define the measures $\nu_N$ and $\mu_N$ by 
\[
\nu_N =\frac{1}{|S_N|} \sum_{A\in S_N} \delta_{u_A\mathbb{Z}^d} \quad\text{and}\quad 
\mu_N=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} a^k_{\ast}\nu_N.
\]
Extracting a subsequences if necessary, we may assume that the sequence $(\mu_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges weak$^\ast$ to some measure $\mu$ on $X$. Note that $\mu$ could be not a probability measure since $X$ is non-compact.

First, observe that $\mu$ is clearly $a$-invariant since $a_\ast \mu_N - \mu_N$ goes to the zero measure. Next, we claim that $\mu$ is a probability measure on $X$ and 
$$\operatorname{Supp}\mu \subset  \{x\in X : \rho_\epsilon \leq \lambda_1(x) \leq \eta_\epsilon \}.$$
Indeed, writing $X(\epsilon) = \{x\in X : \rho_\epsilon \leq \lambda_1(x) \leq \eta_\epsilon \}$,
it follows from the definition of $E(\epsilon)$ that
\[
\mu_N(X\smallsetminus X(\epsilon)) = \frac{1}{N|S_N|} \sum_{A\in S_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \delta_{a^k u_A \mathbb{Z}^{d}} (X\smallsetminus X(\epsilon))
\leq \frac{t_\epsilon}{N}.
\]
By taking $N\to\infty$, we have $\mu(X\smallsetminus X(\epsilon)) = 0$ and the claim follows since $X(\epsilon)$ is compact in $X$.

Finally, we claim that

\begin{equation*}
{
h_\mu (a) \geq m+n-1- \frac{m+n}{mn}\epsilon.
}
\end{equation*}

In order to prove the claim, we fix small $r>0$ which will be determined 
                          
and consider a finite partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ contains an atom $P_\infty$ such that $X\smallsetminus P_\infty$ contains $X(\epsilon)$ and has compact closure;
\item For any $P\in \mathcal{P}\smallsetminus \{P_\infty\}$, $\operatorname{diam} P<r$;
                                                                                
\item For any $P \in \mathcal{P}$, the boundary of $P$ is $\mu$-null, i.e. $\mu(\partial P) =0$.
\end{itemize}
We can build such $\mathcal{P}$ following the procedure in the proof of \cite[Proposition 2.3]{LSS}.
For any $q\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{P}^{(q)} = \bigvee_{k=0}^{q-1}a^{-k}\mathcal{P}$. Write the Euclidean division of large enough $N-1$ by $q$ as
$$N-1=qN' +s \text{ with } s\in \{0,\dots,q-1\}. $$ 
By subadditivity of entropy of the partition it follows that for each $p\in\{0,\dots,q-1\}$ 
\[
H_{\nu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(N)}) \leq H_{a^{p}\nu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(q)}) +H_{a^{p+q}\nu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(q)})+\cdots+H_{a^{p+qN'}\nu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(q)})+2q\log|\mathcal{P}|.
\]
Summing those inequalities for $p=0,\dots,q-1$, and using concavity of entropy of the measure, it follows that
\[
q H_{\nu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(N)}) \leq \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}H_{a^k \nu_N} (\mathcal{P}^{(q)}) + 2q^2 \log|\mathcal{P}| \leq N H_{\mu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(q)}) +2q^2\log|\mathcal{P}|.
\]
Therefore, we have

\begin{equation}
{
\frac{1}{q} H_{\mu_{N}} (\mathcal{P}^{(q)}) \geq \frac{1}{N}H_{\nu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(N)}) -\frac{2q\log|\mathcal{P}|}{N}.
}\label{Eq_entropybound}
\end{equation}


Now we will take $r >0$ small enough. For this denote by $r_1$ the injectivity radius of $X\smallsetminus P_\infty$. See \cite[Proposition 9.14]{EW} for the definition and existence of an injectivity radius. 
Recall the constants $0<r_0<1$ and $C_0\geq 1$ given in the beginning of Section \ref{Sec3}. 
We take $r < \min\{r_0, r_1,C_0^{-1}e^{-\left(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1}{n}\right)}\}$ and claim that for any non-empty atom $P$ of $\mathcal{P}^{(N)}$, there is at most one element $A\in S_N$ such that $u_A\Gamma \in P$.

To prove the claim, suppose that $A_1,A_2\in S_N$ satisfy $u_{A_1}\Gamma, u_{A_2}\Gamma \in P$, that is, $a^ku_{A_1}\Gamma, a^k u_{A_2}\Gamma$ are contained in the same atom of $\mathcal{P}$ for each $k=0,\dots,N-1$. 
It follows from $A_1,A_2 \in E(\epsilon)$ that $a^k u_{A_1}\Gamma, a^k u_{A_2}\Gamma \notin P_\infty$ for all $k\geq t_\epsilon$. In particular, we have
$d_X(a^{N-1} u_{A_1} \Gamma, a^{N-1} u_{A_2} \Gamma) <r$, which implies $d_G(a^{N-1}u_{A_1-A_2}a^{-(N-1)},id) <r$ due to $r<r_1$.
It follows from $r<r_0$ that
\[
d_\infty(a^{N-1}u_{A_1-A_2}a^{-(N-1)},id)=e^{\left(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1}{n}\right)(N-1)}\|A_1-A_2\| < C_0 r,
\]
hence $\|A_1-A_2\| < C_0 r e^{-\left(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1}{n}\right)(N-1)}$. Since $ r< C_0^{-1}e^{-\left(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1}{n}\right)}$ and $A_1,A_2$ are $e^{-\left(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1}{n}\right)N}$-separated, it follows that $A_1=A_2$, which completes the proof of the claim.

It follows from \eqref{Eq_entropybound} and the above claim that 
\[
\frac{1}{q}H_{\mu_N}(\mathcal{P}^{(q)}) \geq \frac{\log |S_N|}{N} -\frac{2q\log|\mathcal{P}|}{N}.
\]
Since the boundary of the atoms of $\mathcal{P}$, hence of $\mathcal{P}^{(q)}$, is of zero $\mu$-measure, taking $N\to\infty$ and using \eqref{Eq_BoxDim}, we have
\[
\frac{1}{q}H_{\mu}(\mathcal{P}^{(q)}) \geq m+n-1-\frac{m+n}{mn}\epsilon.
\] Therefore, we have
\[
h_\mu(a) \geq m+n-1-\frac{m+n}{mn}\epsilon.
\]
head: environment
name: Proof of Proposition \ref{Prop_construction}

title: Proof
body_md:
When $(m,n)=(1,1)$, it follows from \cite[Theorem 1.2]{Kad12}. Assume $(m,n)\neq (1,1)$. Using Proposition \ref{Prop_construction} with $\epsilon=1/k$ for $k\in\mathbb{N}$, we obtain a sequence of $a$-invariant probability measures $(\mu_k)_{k\geq 1}$ on $X$ such that $\operatorname{Supp} \mu_k \subset \{x\in X : \rho_{1/k} \leq \lambda_1(x) \leq \eta_{1/k}\}$ and $h_{\mu_k}(a)\geq m+n-1 -\frac{m+n}{mnk}$. Hence, it follows that $\liminf_{k\to\infty}h_{\mu_k}(a) \geq m+n -1$ and any weak$^\ast$ limit measure is the zero measure since $\rho_{1/k}, \eta_{1/k}\to 0$ as $k\to\infty$. 

On the other hand, if $\limsup_{k\to\infty}h_{\mu_k}(a)>m+n-1$, it follows from Theorem \ref{Thm_KKLM} that there is a subsequence of $(\mu_k)_{k\geq 1}$ such that any weak$^\ast$ limit measure along this subsequence cannot be the zero measure, which is a contradiction. Therefore, $\lim_{k\to\infty}h_{\mu_k}(a) = m+n -1$.

name: Proof of Theorem \ref{Thm_main}

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(\mu_k)_{k\geq 1}$ be as in Theorem ef{Thm_main}. Denote by $m_X$ the Haar probability measure on $X$. 
Note that $h_{m_X} (a) = m+n$ (see e.g. \cite[Theorem 7.9]{EL}). Given $h\in [m+n-1,m+n]$, 
define $$
u_k = (h-(m+n-1))m_X + (m+n-h)\mu_k.$$ 
It follows from \cite[Theorem 2.33]{ELW} that $$h_{
u_k}(a)= (h-(m+n-1))h_{m_X}(a) + (m+n-h)h_{\mu_k}(a),$$ hence $\lim_{k	o\infty}h_{
u_k}(a) =h$. Since the weak$^\ast$ limit measure of $(
u_k)_{k\geq 1}$ is $(h-(m+n-1))m_X$, this completes the proof.
